narration: Black Friday is three weeks away — and stores are already setting the trap. Ninety-two percent of those deals are actually cheaper at other times of the year.
visual: Store exterior at night with giant BLACK FRIDAY SALE banner in amber, animated crowd silhouettes rushing through the doors, '92%' stat counting up in large bold text

narration: Here's the trick: retailers quietly raise prices thirty to forty-five days before Black Friday, then 'slash' them back to normal. That fifty-percent-off tag? It was fifty percent higher last month.
visual: Animated price tag showing price climbing to $400 with an 'OCTOBER PRICE' label, then a '50% OFF — $200' sticker slapping on to reveal the original price was always $200

narration: That door-buster deal and 'only two left' warning trigger your brain's fear center in under three hundred milliseconds — faster than you can read the price. Stores know exactly what they're doing.
visual: Simple brain silhouette with amygdala highlighted in amber, countdown timer ticking fast, pulsing red 'ONLY 2 LEFT!' warning box below

narration: You plan to spend two hundred dollars. The average Black Friday shopper actually spends four hundred ninety-six. Every element of the sale — the timers, the layout, the crowds — is calibrated to do exactly that.
visual: Animated bar chart side by side: green '$200 Planned' bar and amber '$496 Actual' bar growing upward with dollar amounts counting up

narration: And it doesn't stop there. That one day of deals bleeds into weeks of holiday spending. The total? The average American spends fourteen hundred dollars more than they planned, every single holiday season.
visual: Piggy bank SVG with coins falling in from above, dollar counter building from $0 up to $1,400, 'EXTRA EVERY HOLIDAY SEASON' label appearing

narration: Here's the hack: screenshot your wishlist today. In January, sixty percent of those items will be the same price or cheaper — and you'll keep eight hundred dollars in your pocket. Save this.
visual: Phone SVG with screenshot action, arrow pointing to January calendar page, piggy bank filling up in green, '$800 SAVED' badge springing into view
